finding.claim: Blind SSRF: user-supplied callbackUrl is stored with no validation and later POSTed to by the periodic notifier. An attacker can register internal targets (e.g. http://169.254.169.254/, http://localhost:port/admin, internal services) and make the server send POST requests with the payload body to them every minute. Response is discarded, so it is blind, but the request is still made.

trace.note: subscribe(name, callbackUrl) receives the attacker-supplied URL
stored in the subscriptions map without scheme, host or IP validation
notifyAll iterates stored callback URLs on the minute job
URI.create(cb) builds the request URI from the stored value
client.send issues the POST to the attacker-chosen host

finding.guards_checked: No scheme allowlist, host allowlist, private/loopback/link-local IP block, or DNS re-resolution check anywhere on the path. No authentication is visible in this file. HttpClient.newHttpClient() defaults to no redirect following, which only limits redirect-based pivots and does not limit the direct request.

verdict.reason: src/Jobs.java:14 stores callbackUrl unvalidated and src/Jobs.java:21-24 builds URI.create(cb) and sends a POST to it, with no allowlist or IP check anywhere (the only regex guard at :30 protects thumb(), not this path). Only Jobs.java exists, so the /subscribe route is a comment at :12; authentication on it could not be checked.
